Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.

Your Impact

Axon's Air team sells drone and counter-drone systems to police and sheriff's departments. As an Account Executive, you will own the full sales cycle in a territory covering South Texas, Missouri, and Illinois: finding the deal, running it, and closing it yourself. You'll work alongside an Axon Key Account Leader and manage the Skydio partnership piece of your deals, so customers get one integrated solution instead of stitching together vendors. This is a build the market role. You'll be one of the first reps selling this product line in your territory, not inheriting a warm book.

Location: OH

Territory: Indiana, Ohio, Missouri (one combined multi-state territory)

• Manage the Skydio partnership piece of your deals, so customers get one integrated solution instead of stitching together vendors

• Work alongside an Axon Key Account Leader who's already selling other Axon gear into these same departments. You sell Air, they sell the rest, on the same accounts

• Proven success breaking into net-new accounts and winning first-time customers • A track record of hitting or beating quota

• Bachelor's Degree

• Salesforce or equivalent CRM experience

• Willingness to travel 75% of the time within your territory, including overnights. This is a field role, you'll be in police departments, not on Zoom

• Experience selling to government or public-sector buyers is a plus: RFPs, procurement cycles, long sales timelines

• Familiarity with drone, cloud, or virtualization technology is a plus

Benefits that Benefit You

• Discretionary paid time off

• Paid parental leave for all

• Learning & Development programs

8+ years of product management experience with deep emphasis on AI / agents.

•
3+ years of tax experience — as a tax practitioner and/or building tax products for the CPA or corporate tax market.

•
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with a track record of cross-functional collaboration.

•
Comfortable with ambiguity which comes with launching new products.

•
Degree in a technical, accounting, or related field, or equivalent professional experience.

More about Fieldguide

Fieldguide is a values-based company. Our values are:

•
Fearless - Inspire & break down seemingly impossible walls.

•
Fast - Launch fast with excellence, iterate to perfection.

•
Lovable - Deliver happiness & 11 star experiences.

Competitive compensation packages with meaningful ownership

jobs.title: SOX AI Specialist (Contractor)
jobs.sourceName: Jobicy: latest jobs
jobs.description:
About us

Fieldguide is establishing a new state of trust for global commerce and capital markets by automating and streamlining the work of advisory, audit, and tax practitioners at the world’s largest CPA firms. Put simply, we build software for the people who enable trust between businesses.

We’re headquartered in San Francisco, California, and backed by top investors, including Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Bessemer Venture Partners, 8VC, Floodgate, Y Combinator, DNX Ventures, Global Founders Capital, Justin Kan, Elad Gil, and others.

About the Engagement

We are seeking an experienced SOX and internal controls practitioner for a paid, short-term contract engagement. This is not a full-time role (at this time).

Over an initial engagement of 8–12 weeks, with the potential to extend, you will work directly with a small, cross-functional group of subject-matter experts, AI engineers, and product partners. You’ll help translate real-world SOX testing judgment into reliable, AI-assisted workflows. This is not a traditional client-delivery audit or attestation role. Your focus will be on prompting and refining AI agents to execute control testing and partnering closely with AI engineers to identify new engineering capabilities to enable better control testing.

Engagement type: Direct contractor

Initial term: 8–12 weeks, with potential to extend

Start date: Immediate

Time commitment: Approximately 40 hours per week

Target rate: $60–$80 per hour, based on experience, with flexibility for an exceptional fit .

What You’ll Do

•
Partner closely with engineering, product, and design teams to translate real-world SOX testing processes into scalable product capabilities .

•
Co-develop AI agents with AI engineers to execute detailed SOX testing by translating SOX testing methodology into specific guidance, decision rules, and examples.

•
Work hands-on with AI agents: write and refine prompts, run controls and evidence through testing workflows, evaluate outputs, and document failure modes.

•
Analyze risk and control matrices and test plans to identify opportunities for improved agentic testing.

•
Develop stress-test scenarios, review and assess AI agent performance , and create detailed error analyses and evaluation criteria.

What We’re Looking For

•
At least four years of hands-on control testing experience in SOX compliance, internal audit, or internal controls, with direct responsibility for control design and testing.

•
Broad experience across a range of control types, industries, and firms, with clear expertise in business process control testing.

•
The ability to consistently explain why a test step, exception, or conclusion passes or fails and to turn that reasoning into clear evaluation criteria.

•
Strong written reasoning: you can explain workflows and decisions step by step and turn professional judgment into clear rules, edge cases, and review criteria.

•
A high degree of comfort and hands-on experience using AI tools, writing prompts, and working with agentic harnesses.

•
Comfort operating in ambiguity, testing ideas quickly, and changing your approach when the evidence does not support it.

•
Availability for the expected time commitment during the initial engagement.

What We’d Love to See

•
Experience at the senior or manager level reviewing SOX workpapers or coaching testers.

•
A CPA, CIA, or similar relevant credential.

•
Experience across multiple companies, clients, industries, or control environments.

•
Familiarity with both business process controls and ITGCs.

•
Demonstrated interest or experience in creating AI workflows or tools of any kind.

Company Description

Palmetto is a consumer energy platform that provides homeowners with a single destination to discover, purchase, finance, install, monitor and manage home energy products and services. Palmetto prioritizes people, planet, and profit—backed by a culture that values collaboration, impact, and balance. Join us in building a brighter, cleaner world.

Department Description

Service Operations is a core function within Palmetto’s Service and Asset Management organization, responsible for post-PTO service and maintenance across the residential solar asset lifecycle. The team ensures system performance, reliability, and customer satisfaction by managing service requests from intake through resolution. This includes remote troubleshooting, site visit coordination, and field execution through both in-house technicians and a national network of service partners.

Service Operations plays a critical role in protecting asset performance and optimizing the cost of service at scale. Our focus is to resolve issues quickly, efficiently, and with high quality—balancing speed, cost, and customer satisfaction while supporting the long-term performance of the assets we manage.

Location

This position will be based remotely in the Philippines.

The Tech Support Specialist I is responsible for monitoring system performance and resolving service issues through remote troubleshooting across Palmetto’s residential solar portfolio.

This role is the first line of defense in identifying and addressing system underperformance, using monitoring tools, diagnostics, and customer interaction to resolve issues without requiring a site visit whenever possible.

Tech Support Specialists are accountable for quickly identifying root causes, executing effective troubleshooting steps, and determining when escalation to a site visit is necessary. They play a critical role in optimizing service timelines, reducing cost of service, and ensuring a seamless customer experience.

• Monitor system performance across the residential solar portfolio, proactively identifying underperforming or non-producing systems through alerting and diagnostic tools.

• Execute remote troubleshooting steps to resolve system issues, including inverter resets, communication troubleshooting, and guiding homeowners through required actions.

• Maximize remote resolution by identifying and applying effective solutions, minimizing unnecessary site visits.

• Communicate clearly and empathetically with homeowners to explain issues, guide troubleshooting steps, and set expectations for resolution.

• Accurately document all troubleshooting steps, findings, and outcomes within Salesforce to ensure clear case history and enable downstream coordination if needed.

• Escalate unresolved or complex issues to Service Project Coordinators with clear, complete context, including validated scope and recommended next steps.

• Manage and prioritize service queues to ensure all cases are addressed within defined SLA timelines.

• Identify trends, recurring issues, and failure patterns across the portfolio, contributing insights to improve monitoring, processes, and product performance.

• Collaborate cross-functionally with Service Operations, Product, and Engineering teams to improve alert quality, reduce false positives, and enhance troubleshooting workflows.

• Participate in root cause analysis and continuous improvement initiatives to increase remote resolution rates and reduce overall service cost.

Qualifications

• BS/BA is preferred.

• 2+ years of experience in technical support, customer support, or operations in a high-volume environment.

• Spanish proficiency is required.

• Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills, with the ability to diagnose issues using data and structured thinking.

• Ability to quickly learn and navigate monitoring platforms, CRM systems, and technical tools (Salesforce experience preferred).

• Strong communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts clearly to non-technical customers.

Reporting to APAC Marketing, you will be our first dedicated marketing hire in Japan and a key part of the Japan team led by our Country Manager. You will drive pipeline, accelerate deals and build brand presence in one of the fastest-growing contact center markets in the world, while staying closely aligned with Cresta's global marketing strategy and campaigns. • In partnership with APAC Marketing, develop and execute Cresta's Japan marketing plan, aligned to both Japan pipeline goals and global marketing priorities

• Translate global campaigns and product launches into effective Japan execution plans

• Own and execute field marketing in Japan, including planning and running in-market events from target list and invitations through on-site execution and follow-up

• Partner closely with Japan Sales to drive pipeline creation and acceleration

• Act as the primary bridge between Japan Sales and APAC and Global Marketing

• Provide Japan insights to inform global messaging, campaigns and roadmap decisions

• Partner with Product Marketing on localization and content so that presentations, web content, sales materials and customer stories are on brand and effectively translated

• Coordinate press and media activity in Japan with ourGlobal Corporate Communications Director, APAC Marketing Director and our selected in-country PR partner. This will include announcements, approved customer stories, and media and analyst briefings

Design and run experiments with our Senior SEO/GEO Specialist to learn what moves visibility in LLMs, and document what you find.

B2B SaaS or demand generation experience

A product worth recommending. Operations teams in factories, fleets, hospitals and campuses already choose MaintainX, so you'll be earning visibility for something customers love.

Autodesk scale, same mission. As part of Autodesk, we have more resources and reach, pointed at the problem we were already solving.

jobs.description:
About Docplanner and Noa

Docplanner is a global healthcare platform connecting more than 300,000 doctors with approximately 100 million patients every month across 13 markets.

Within Docplanner, Noa is on a mission to help people live longer, healthier lives. We build AI that works alongside doctors to:

•
Remove their administrative work.

•
Help them make better decisions and handle repeatable cases, so they can spend their time where it matters most.

•
Help patients navigate healthcare using their medical history as personalized context.

We're already in doctors' hands: Noa Notes takes documentation off their plates, while Noa Evidence brings trustworthy medical evidence to the point of care.

The next frontier is the hardest—and the most valuable: helping doctors, and eventually patients, make decisions while our AI safely takes on repeatable clinical work. That's where a doctor's judgment has to live inside the product itself. That's this role.

About the role

You’ll help take Noa from writing notes and providing evidence to helping doctors decide—ensuring what we build fits clinical workflows and earns doctors’ trust.

This isn’t a traditional CMO, advisory or regulatory role. It is a hands-on, individual-contributor clinical-product role. You will:

•
Shape doctor-facing products by bringing real clinical needs and workflows into product decisions.

•
Bring clinical judgment to what we build, including what is correct, useful and safe.

Because you’re a doctor yourself, you can talk to our users peer-to-peer and get the honest answers a survey never will. As our first dedicated clinical hire on the product, you’ll help establish how clinical expertise informs Docplanner’s AI products.

You’ll work day-to-day with Product, AI, Design, Engineering, Regulatory and our doctor network.

What you’ll do

Shape what we build

•
Bring how doctors really work—their habits, workflows and administrative realities—into the product.

•
Talk to doctors across specialties and working styles, and turn candid feedback into product decisions.

•
Partner with Product, Design and Engineering to prioritise and ship improvements, then learn from how doctors use them.

Bring clinical judgment into the product

•
Help define what correct, useful and safe looks like for our doctor-facing AI products.

•
Review prompts, outputs, clinical templates and workflows, and identify clinically meaningful failure modes.

•
Turn clinician feedback and evaluation findings into product and model improvements with Product, ML/LLM and evaluation partners.

Keep it safe and scalable

•
Work with Product, ML/LLM, Regulatory and the PRRC to align product intent, evidence, risks and controls.

•
Build practical feedback loops with practising clinicians and our consultant-doctor network.

What we’re looking for

•
A medical degree and at least 2 years of direct clinical practice. Active licensure and current practice are not required.

•
Meaningful experience shaping and shipping a doctor-facing or clinical product, either as a clinical product leader or a clinician-founder/builder.

•
You personally owned product decisions, worked directly with Product, Design and Engineering, and shipped something clinicians used.

•
You’ve turned clinical problems into product decisions—not just provided advice, review or governance.

•
You combine strong clinical judgment with doctor discovery, workflow understanding and a focus on trust and adoption.

•
You communicate clearly and directly across clinical, product, technical, regulatory and leadership teams.

•
You’re comfortable operating independently as a senior, hands-on contributor in a lean cross-functional team.

•
You actively use generative AI and understand its potential and limitations. Hands-on experience with prompting, output review or AI-assisted development tools is valuable.

Bonus: Experience with ambient documentation, clinical templates, medical-knowledge systems, clinical coding or regulated Software as a Medical Device.

What success looks like after 6 months

•
A clear, evidence-backed view of the priority doctor workflows and product opportunities Noa should address.

•
Product improvements shipped based on doctor discovery, feedback and observed usage.

•
Clear clinical quality expectations and feedback loops established with Product, ML/LLM and evaluation partners.

Why join Noa at Docplanner

•
Real impact at real scale: Your work reaches hundreds of thousands of doctors and their patients.

•
Shape what comes next: You’ll influence what Noa and Docplanner’s AI products become—and whether doctors and patients trust them.

•
Ship to learn: A feature in front of users beats another month of planning.

•
Work flexibly: The role is 100% remote across eligible European locations, subject to local hiring arrangements.

Our advocacy arm, Bobbie for Change, exists because making great formula isn't enough if the systems around parenthood are still broken. Head of Content
Outmarket AI · Remote (US) · Full-time · Reports to the SVP of Marketing

About Outmarket
Insurance still runs on manual work. Most policies are sold through agents and brokers, and the people who know the work best are buried in the documents: checking policies line by line, comparing quotes, building proposals, on nights and weekends. We think that's backwards. The best people in insurance should spend their time advising clients.
Outmarket, the AI platform built for insurance, makes that possible. Account teams drop in their documents and get back finished work to review, with every finding linked to the page it came from. Outmarket connects to the systems they already use. The judgment stays with the person; the groundwork doesn't.
It's working. More than 10,000 people at over 300 agencies use Outmarket, including 30 of the top 100 U.S. insurance brokers. Most of those agencies found us through other customers. We raised a $34.5M Series B led by SignalFire four months after announcing our Series A because customers were pulling us forward faster than we planned.

Why this role

• Customers who want to talk. About 300 agencies use Outmarket, and most will go on record about it. Few content leaders start with that many stories ready to tell.

• First in the seat. You'll be our first content hire, joining alongside a new Head of Product Marketing and Head of Growth. You'll decide what Outmarket sounds and looks like.

• Real creative room, and a budget to use it. There's budget for specialist contractors such as editors, shooters and designers, and you'll have room to make work that doesn't look like typical B2B content.

• A direct line. You'll work with the SVP of Marketing, the founders and customers, and you'll see what your work does for pipeline within weeks.

The role
You own video, social, customer stories and written content. You'll build the function hands-on: you script, interview, direct and write yourself, and you work with a small group of specialist contractors instead of an in-house crew. Pipeline is the team's main number, so success means content that brings brokers into sales conversations, not just views.
Our buyers are owners, producers and operations leaders at commercial insurance agencies. It's a relationship-driven industry, and we're still learning where these buyers spend their attention online. Part of your job is finding out, then making the content that reaches them there.

What you'll do

• Run the customer story program. Choose which customers to feature with our client services team, plan each story before the shoot, run the interview, and cut one day of filming into pieces for the website, ads, sales and events. Make it easy for busy customers to say yes, and never over-ask the same ones.

• Ship every week. Build a steady publishing rhythm with a bench of specialist contractors. Find them, brief them clearly, know what things should cost, and review closely so quality holds as volume grows.

• Turn our events into content. Work with our Director of Industry Events & Programs to plan what to capture at the conferences and customer dinners we already run, and publish soon after.

• Find where brokers pay attention, whether that's LinkedIn, YouTube, industry media or events. Put our effort where the audience is, not where content teams usually start.

• Build leaders' voices. Help our founders and other leaders post every week, each in their own voice.

• Own written content, including the site, social and long-form pieces, and keep everything we publish clear and sharp.

• Measure what your content does for pipeline and use that to decide what to make next.

What we're looking for

• 5+ years in B2B content, brand or creative, including time owning a content program end to end.

• You've personally made content that grew an audience or produced demos and pipeline, and you can explain the numbers and your part in them.

• You're a hands-on maker. You've scripted, directed, interviewed and edited video and social content yourself, not only managed an agency or writers.

• You've produced customer stories people actually watch, and you know how to run a great interview.

• You've shipped on a small budget with contractors and can say what each piece cost.

• You've built content at an early-stage company, ideally Series A to C, and want to build from scratch again.

• You're an excellent writer.

How we work

• High agency: you find the work instead of waiting for it.

• Ownership: you own the outcome, not a task list.

• Startup pace: we ship weekly instead of planning quarterly.

You don't need to know insurance. Curiosity about brokers is the requirement, and becoming fluent is part of the job.

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/outmarket-ai-head-of-content

We're hiring a Nurse Practitioner to serve as the primary clinical point of contact for patients navigating their remote care journey.

In this role, you will lead clinical decision-making with a strong emphasis on guideline-directed medical therapy for heart failure, as well as adherence to evidence-based guidelines for type 2 diabetes and hypertension, including proactive and asynchronous medication titration based on patient vitals, symptoms, and trends. This role requires a high level of clinical autonomy, strong judgment, and close collaboration with Registered Nurses and Patient Success teams to deliver timely, patient-centered, and scalable remote care.

Money is moving onto the internet, and the shift has a name: Open Money. This is money that is open, portable, agentic, and owned by you. MetaMask spent the last ten years building it; with 100M+ downloads, users in ~190 countries, and trillions in cumulative transaction volume, it's the most trusted self-custodial financial platform on the internet. Now we're building the operating system for your money: one place to hold, move, grow, and use anything you own. Join a remote-first, global team rebuilding how money works: a problem that touches everyone, every day.

About MetaMask & Trade

MetaMask is a self-custodial wallet used by tens of millions of people. In Trade, people swap, bridge, trade perps, predict and earn. Core UX is the part of MetaMask mobile that sit inside: Home, the navigation, balances, tokens and positions, and the path from the first screen into each of them.

People open the app and land on Home. If that screen is slow, crowded, or unclear about what to do next, Swap, Perps, Predict and Earn see fewer of the people who opened the app. The surface is live. You start from the app people already have, and you keep shipping on it.

The role is Staff Product Manager, Core UX. You write the vision for Home and the navigation, and you run the build with design and engineering. A design background is a requirement, because the work is the screen itself.

The Role

You are the product manager for Core UX on MetaMask mobile. You own the vision, the roadmap and the backlog for Home and the navigation, and you own whether that screen is working.

You will work closely with:

• The Core UX engineering team

• Design

• Data and analytics

• The product managers for Swap, Perps, Predict and Earn

Those products show up on Home. You own how a person reaches them from there, and how their balances and positions show up. Their roadmaps stay with their product managers. Yours is Home and the navigation.

The app is already live and people open it every day, so you start from what is there. You walk design leadership through the screen, and you are in the reviews where the layout gets decided.

What You'll Do

Set the Core UX vision

Write what Home is for, who has to succeed on it, and what it shows before anyone taps. Getting back to an open position has to be fast for people who already trade here. A first install still has to reach one real action in that same session.

Write down where a MetaMask person would already know what to tap, and where one of those apps does something we should study. Then write the roadmap, with the tradeoffs and the order, and what each step changes on Home.

Own Home, the navigation and the defaults

Own what a person sees when they open the app. That is balances, tokens and positions, and the way into Swap, Perps, Predict and Earn. A balance, a token, a position and an entry point are different, and Home has to show each one in a place the person can find.

Decide what Home shows before anyone taps. Anything past that waits until the person opens it. Put Swap, Perps and Predict close together for people who use more than one of them. A person using only one of those products still has to be able to finish their action.

Search and any assistance that sits on Home are part of this surface. You specify what stays on the screen, and what the person still confirms before money moves.

Get people to a first action, and get them to come back

You own the first session and the return after it. Count how many new wallets take a real action, and how many of those people open the app again. Define the path from the open to a confirmed action, and instrument it.

Review screens with design

You have a design background, and the role uses it. You review screens for hierarchy, type, spacing and what a tap does. You mark up a screen and say what should change, in writing, so design and engineering can build from the note.

You write the product point of view clearly enough that design and engineering can build it. You are in the design reviews. A crowded screen, or a tap that does the wrong thing, gets the specific change you want.

Work with the products that live on Home

Each MetaMask trade primitive already has their own product manager. You own the entry from Home and the way their positions and balances read there. When a change to Home helps one product and hurts another, you name the tradeoff in the spec.

You coordinate the sequencing when a Home change depends on one of those teams, or when one of their launches depends on Home. The spec says what Home will show on the day their change ships.

Join the Tilt team
At Tilt, we see a side of people that traditional lenders miss. The Opportunity: Manager, Strategic Sourcing
Tilt is hiring its first Strategic Sourcing lead, with the opportunity to establish strategic sourcing as a function and practice at the company. The core of the role is commercial judgment and hands-on negotiation: you'll quickly understand what each team needs, assess vendor economics, and secure the best pricing and terms across the US and our international markets in Latin America and Asia. You'll focus your time on negotiations and measurable savings, keeping requirements gathering and vendor selection proportionate to the decision. Our spend spans banking and payments, credit and identity data, cloud and software, marketing, servicing and collections, and contractors and professional services. In this senior, hands-on role, you'll partner closely with Compliance, Legal, and Finance, help prepare Tilt for an initial public offering (IPO), and typically run five or more sourcing projects at a time.

How You’ll Make an Impact

• Lead supplier negotiations : Own negotiations from new contracts to renewals and usage-based pricing, using should-cost models, market benchmarks, and competing bids to win better pricing and terms.

• Apply practical commercial judgment: Work with business owners to identify essential needs quickly, challenge unnecessary scope, and evaluate pricing, usage commitments, and total cost. Use targeted market checks or competitive bids where useful, and formal RFPs only when the complexity or value of the purchase warrants them.

• Apply zero-based vendor budgeting: Partner with Finance and business owners to justify vendor spend from current needs, expected usage, and business value rather than carrying forward last year's budget. Challenge renewals and minimum commitments, and identify services to eliminate, consolidate, or right-size.

• Set global category strategy : Manage spend by category across the US and our international markets, consolidate suppliers and negotiate global agreements where it lowers cost or risk, and set simple rules for small, one-off purchases.

• Build a simple sourcing and vendor management process: Partner with Legal, Compliance, IT, and Finance to design an easy-to-use workflow from vendor intake and onboarding through ongoing reviews, renewals, and offboarding. Establish clear owners, approval thresholds, risk-based reviews, and turnaround expectations so teams can navigate legal, compliance, and IT requirements without unnecessary handoffs. Build a practical negotiation playbook and coach teams on how to buy well.

• Make negotiated savings real: Partner with Finance and Accounts Payable on contract-to-invoice reviews, checking billed rates, usage, discounts, credits, and price increases against agreed terms. Resolve discrepancies with vendors, recover overcharges, and track realized savings against an agreed baseline.

• Make procurement IPO-ready : Put in place public-company controls, including purchase approvals, segregation of duties, contract records, and audit trails that support Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) compliance.

• Improve the tools and data : Contribute to Tilt's procure-to-pay (P2P) and contract lifecycle management (CLM) processes alongside Finance and Legal, keep contract and renewal records current, and use AI tools to speed up contract review and spend analysis.

In 1933, Harry Beck introduced a radically different map of the London Underground. Rather than faithfully depicting the geography of London, he simplified the sprawling transit network into clean lines, clear connections, and a system that anyone could navigate. Distances were distorted, angles were standardized, and unnecessary details disappeared. The result was something far more useful than a geographically accurate map: a way for millions of people to understand a complex system and confidently find their way through it.

Beck understood something fundamental. The best way to explain something complicated isn't to show people everything. It's to understand what matters to them and make that unmistakably clear.

At Mercury, we believe great product marketing works the same way. Banking* and payments can be complex, but the value they create for customers shouldn't be. Our job is to understand what people need, find the essence of what we're building, and help customers see how it can make their lives better.

We're a financial technology company building products that help ambitious businesses do more with their money. From everyday banking and payments to international money movement and emerging capabilities like agentic payments, we're making complex financial workflows feel remarkably simple.

We're looking for a Product Marketing Manager to help bring these products to market, communicate their value, and make sure customers discover and use what we're building.

This role sits at the intersection of Product, Marketing, and Revenue. You'll develop positioning, lead go-to-market strategies, drive successful product launches, and identify opportunities to increase adoption and revenue.

Its Clinical Intelligence takes on the routine, high-volume work of chronic care – monitoring patients, surfacing risks, and coordinating action – so clinicians can focus on the decisions that require them. Grounded in partnerships with more than 20 leading health systems, deep EMR integrations, dedicated medical group, and experience serving a population of more than 100,000 patients, the system learns from real-world care delivery, improving as it scales. Cadence has been recognized by TIME as one of the Top 100 HealthTech Companies and by LinkedIn as a Top Startup (#4, 2025).

The Role

We're hiring a Nurse Practitioner to serve as the primary clinical point of contact for patients navigating their remote care journey.

In this role, you will lead clinical decision-making with a strong emphasis on guideline-directed medical therapy for heart failure, as well as adherence to evidence-based guidelines for type 2 diabetes and hypertension, including proactive and asynchronous medication titration based on patient vitals, symptoms, and trends. You will oversee patients, manage clinical escalations, and collaborate closely with the patient’s physician or provider to optimize treatment plans, adjust medications, and determine the appropriate level of care. This role requires a high level of clinical autonomy, strong judgment, and close collaboration with Registered Nurses and Patient Success teams to deliver timely, patient-centered, and scalable remote care.

Although this position is fully remote, it is a highly collaborative, fast-paced clinical role with clear expectations for productivity, responsiveness, and quality.

Licensure Requirements

Required: Active Compact Multi-State RN license.

Required: Active NP licensure in MS.

Licenses must be active and in good standing at time of hire.

Schedule Requirements

This role is fully remote. Monday through Friday schedule with a core shift schedule of 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM Central Time.

What You'll Do

• Manage a panel of patients receiving remote care, making timely clinical decisions based on evidence-based guidelines for heart failure, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes.

• Deliver high-quality, evidence-based care by following established clinical protocols and workflows while applying sound clinical judgment to individual patient needs.

• Initiate and titrate guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) while collaborating closely with physicians, RNs, and care teams to optimize outcomes.

• Respond promptly to clinical escalations generated through remote patient monitoring, including abnormal vitals, symptoms, and laboratory results.

• Provide both synchronous and asynchronous patient care, including reviewing patient-generated health data, responding to remote patient monitoring alerts, communicating through secure messaging, and conducting scheduled virtual visits when appropriate.

• Deliver safe, efficient, high-quality care while consistently meeting established productivity and documentation expectations.

• Adapt quickly to evolving workflows, software enhancements, and operational processes as we continuously improve our care model.

• Use multiple technology platforms confidently and provide feedback that helps improve our clinical operations and technology.

• Collaborate across clinical and operational teams to identify opportunities to improve patient care, efficiency, and scalability.

• Help shape the future of a rapidly growing digital health organization where every team member contributes to building better processes—not simply following established ones.

These responsibilities are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by personnel assigned to this job classification. About Customer.io

Over 8,000 companies — from scrappy startups to global brands — use our platform to send billions of emails, push notifications, in-app messages, and SMS every day. Customer.io powers automated communication that people actually want to receive. We help teams send smarter, more relevant messages using real-time behavioral data.

About the role

Hi, I’m Matt Lane, Sr. Manager of Account Management at Customer.io , and I’m hiring a Sr. Account Manager to join our EMEA team. This is a sales role. You’ll own a portfolio of mid-market and enterprise customers and be accountable for generating expansion pipeline, closing new revenue, and securing renewals.

You’ll build on existing customer relationships and prospect beyond them. That means cold calling people who haven’t worked with us, identifying new buying teams, and winning business with additional brands within the same parent company. You’ll lead discovery, build relationships with multiple stakeholders, and own each deal from the first conversation through negotiation and close.

We’re looking for someone with a track record in B2B sales who can walk us through an expansion deal they sourced and closed. You should be comfortable generating your own pipeline, multi-threading across complex accounts, and using a sales methodology such as MEDDICC to qualify opportunities and move deals forward.

This role is open to candidates based in the UK or Ireland only.

What we value

• Commercial ownership — you treat your book of business like it's yours, because it is

• Forecasting discipline and data-driven decision-making, not gut feel

• Multi-threaded relationships — you build trust across the org, not just with one champion

• Expansion through value, not feature gates or mechanical levers

• Close partnership with Customer Success — you see CS as a collaborator, not a handoff

What you'll do

• Own the full commercial strategy for a portfolio of mid-market and enterprise accounts — renewals, expansion, and churn mitigation

• Drive growth by helping customers adopt Customer.io more strategically, identifying new use cases and articulating ROI clearly

• Forecast renewal and expansion pipeline accurately with a clear, repeatable methodology

• Build multi-threaded relationships from day-to-day operators to Directors and VPs, becoming a trusted commercial advisor

• Partner closely with Customer Success on account health and with Sales on expansion deals

• Engage Legal and Finance on complex renewals and collaborate cross-functionally to move deals forward

What we're looking for

• 3+ years in Sr. Account Management, Sales, or a related SaaS commercial role with direct ownership of a revenue number (5+ years preferred)

• Experience managing $5m ARR, predominantly in the MM space

• Proven ability to grow customer spend outside of overages or true-ups — genuine expansion through adoption and value articulation

• A forecasting methodology you can walk through clearly — it doesn't need to be a named framework, just logic you own

• Comfortable pulling usage data, tracking health scores, and building your own dashboards

• Strong communicator — clear and persuasive with both technical and non-technical stakeholders

• Based in the UK or Ireland

Compensation & Benefits

We believe in transparency. Starting salary for this role is $142,900 - $171,000 OTE USD (or equivalent in your local currency) depending on experience and subject to market rate adjustment. This role is a 70/30 OTE split. In addition to base salary, this role includes an equity grant in the form of stock options, so you share in the success you help build.

We know our people are what make us great, and we're committed to taking great care of them. Our inclusive benefits package supports your well-being and growth, including 100% coverage of medical, dental, vision, mental health, and supplemental insurance premiums for you and your family . We also offer 16 weeks paid parental leave, unlimited PTO , stipends for remote work and wellness, a professional development budget, and more.

See full benefits here →

Our Process

No gotchas, no trick questions - just a clear, human process designed to help both of us make an informed decision.

• 30-minute video call with a Recruiter

• 45-minute video call with the Hiring Manager

• Take-Home Assignment

• 1-hour Assignment Review Call with the team

All final candidates will be asked to complete a background check and employment verifications as part of our pre-employment process.

Join us!

Check out our careers page for more information about why you should come work with us! We believe in empathy, transparency, responsibility, and, yes, a little awkwardness. If you're excited by what you read — apply now.

jobs.sourceName: RSS: We Work Remotely: All Jobs
jobs.description:
Headquarters: Remote (U.S.)

Discord has a highly engaged community of millions of daily active users who use the platform for many different reasons, but there’s one thing that nearly everyone does: play video games. Discord plays a uniquely important role in the future of gaming, and we are focused on making it easier and more fun for people to hang out before, during, and after playing games.

Discord is hiring a Director of User Experience Research to lead our research team, drive a user-centered understanding of Players (the people who use Discord), and turn that understanding into a better product. You'll own the research strategy for Discord, build and lead a team of researchers, and make sure a deep, evidence-based understanding of user needs shapes what we build before decisions are made.

You'll uncover and forecast the problems our users face and the opportunities that will add the most value to Discord. You'll deepen our understanding of every user cohort, from longtime gamers to new communities, creators, moderators, and teens. And you'll make sure what we ship results in user value for them. As Discord brings more AI-powered experiences to users, you'll ensure they're grounded in real needs and held to a clear, user-centered quality bar. You'll also modernize how research gets done, using AI to increase our speed and reach without losing rigor.

You'll partner closely with Product, Design, Engineering, Data Science, and Safety. This person will report to the VP of Product Design and Insights.

What You'll Be Doing

• Set the research vision and make research a strategic partner. Own the research roadmap across Discord, balancing foundational, generative, and evaluative work and prioritizing by user impact, business impact, and risk. Deliver clear, compelling readouts that shape prioritization and go/no-go calls, and measure research's impact on product outcomes.

• Uncover opportunities and build a shared understanding of our users. Lead foundational and generative research that surfaces unmet needs, pain points, and emerging behaviors, and use segmentation, longitudinal, and international research to understand how different user cohorts use Discord and where their needs differ, so teams design for real people instead of assumptions.

• Own usability and concept validation. Establish a consistent program for testing concepts, prototypes, and live experiences, so teams learn early whether ideas are desirable, usable, and valuable before investing heavily.

• Bring a mixed-methods lens to every major decision. Partner with Data Science to combine qualitative insight with quantitative evidence (surveys, behavioral data, experimentation) that explains both what users do and why. Define and track experience-health measures such as satisfaction, ease, and trust over time.

• Define user-centered quality for AI-powered experiences. Work with Product, Engineering, and ML partners to set quality dimensions, rubrics, and human evaluation programs that complement automated and model-based evaluation, so AI features solve real Player problems and earn user trust.

• Build and scale the practice. Hire and develop researchers and research leads, and create the career paths, rituals, and research operations they need. Equip PMs and designers to run lightweight research with the right guardrails.

• Modernize research with care and integrity. Adopt and govern AI-assisted tools for recruiting, moderation, synthesis, and insight management that help the team move faster and reach more users. Set the standard for ethical research, including rigor, bias, privacy, consent, and research with teens and vulnerable communities, in partnership with Legal, Privacy, and Safety.

What you should have

• 12+ years of experience in UX research or a closely related field (such as HCI, Psychology, or Cognitive Science), including 6+ years leading researchers and research leads

• Deep expertise across generative and evaluative methods, both qualitative and quantitative, with the judgment to turn ambiguous questions into a clear set of risks and design right-sized research for fast-moving product contexts

• A track record of research that uncovered new opportunities and changed product direction, not only validated existing plans, including usability and concept-testing programs that teams relied on

• Experience understanding and segmenting diverse user populations, ideally in consumer social, community, communication, or multi-sided platforms

• Experience researching AI or LLM-powered products, including human evaluation, rubric design, and inter-rater reliability, with a clear view of where automated evaluation helps and where it falls short

• Fluency with AI-enabled research and data tools, and sound judgment about when they strengthen research and when they weaken it

• A history of earning buy-in from executives and cross-functional partners by telling the user story and making the "so what" impossible to ignore

About the role:
An indispensable component of Clipboard's marketplace is its workplace customers. The Customer Success Manager ensures the continued success of the partnership between Clipboard and its workplace partners, working to deliver an optimal experience at every level of their organizations. The job encompasses being a resource to workplaces when issues arise, liaising with building- and corporate-level contacts, and keeping abreast of a litany of important business metrics for each account.
Your week will be balanced between high-touch customer engagement and internal account strategy, with a laser focus on net revenue retention. You are an avid problem-solver, a strategic communicator, and a diligent executor who can navigate complex relationships to sharpen your business acumen.
Responsibilities:

• Manage & grow your portfolio: Own a book of business with accountability for "Same-Store Shift Postings" (SSSP, which measures utilization) and "Same-Store Net Revenue" (SSNR, which measures profitability). In your pursuit of driving those numbers higher, you will identify churn risks, mitigate issues, and proactively uncover opportunities for commercial expansion.

• Strategic account planning: Build and maintain detailed account plans. Forecast performance accurately and provide regular insights to internal leadership regarding pipeline health and account stability.

• Drive executive value: Establish trust with both clinical and non-clinical executives. Lead Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) and strategic meetings to demonstrate value, align on business goals, and negotiate mutually beneficial outcomes.

• Operational excellence: Act as the primary point of contact for complex escalations, ensuring rapid resolution while implementing systemic solutions to prevent recurrence.

• Cross-functional advocacy: Partner with Product, Legal, and Strategy Operations to represent the voice of the customer, driving product improvements and internal initiatives that optimize the client experience.

Beyond the basics, what will make you successful:

• Extreme ownership : The buck stops with you, no matter what anyone else did or did not do. You're self-reliant, and can get things done in the chaos that is an early-stage startup scaling quickly.

• Extreme curiosity : You ask "why" 3-5 times in a row for the same problem, digging and digging and not being satisfied until you truly understand the root cause.

• Scrappiness : You look for ways through problems and refuse to let obstacles derail your progress. You bring solutions instead of asking ‘what should I do?’

• Fast-paced : You thrive on moving quickly and are highly adaptable to a market that evolves quickly.

Our interview process:

• Application (where you are now!)

• Case study

• Interview 1 with a hiring manager

• Interview 2 with Head of Account Management

• Culture chat with a partner on our People Team

Why a case study first?
Since this role is remote and requires a high degree of autonomy, the case study helps us understand how you operate in an asynchronous environment. Specifically, we’re looking at how you interpret written context, navigate ambiguity, and identify opportunities independently. This ensures our first conversation is grounded in your actual work style rather than just a resume walkthrough.

• Relationship management experience not required but strongly preferred

• Excellent verbal and written communication skills

• Willingness to try / lack of fear

• Bachelor's Degree

Benefits:

• Do great work that matters for customers who could really use your help

• Competitive pay

• Unlimited PTO

• Fully Remote

Clipboard would never ask you for money or your bank details to participate in our hiring process. Report any scammers impersonating the Clipboard hiring team members here .

Acquisition works today but is concentrated in a few paid channels. Lifecycle and cross-sell are early, and the brand is under-measured. This is a chance to build an AI-native growth function in one of Latin America's largest and fastest-moving consumer credit markets.

• Grow customer value through lifecycle and cross-sell: Build triggered campaigns across push, SMS, WhatsApp, email and in-app that move customers from first loan to repeat loans, installment loans and the credit card. Partner with Product and Engineering to define what the lifecycle stack needs, and own the strategy that runs on it.

• Run a small, leveraged team: Lead a tight, high-output team that uses AI for creative production, budget allocation and analytics rather than defaulting to headcount growth. Share what works with the growth teams in our other markets: the US, Brazil, India and the Philippines.

Why you're a great fit

• You've had real budget accountability: your name on spend decisions, not just advisory input.

• Consumer fintech or digital lending experience in Mexico or Latin America. You understand how acquisition cost, approval rates and credit losses shape what growth is worth.

• Strong quantitative fluency. CAC, LTV (lifetime value), payback, attribution models and A/B test design (sample size, statistical significance) are second nature.

About Upstart

At Upstart, we’re united by a mission that matters: to radically reduce the cost and complexity of borrowing for all Americans. Every day, we bring creativity, experimentation, and advanced AI to reshape access to credit, helping millions move forward financially with clarity and confidence.

As the leading AI lending marketplace, we partner with banks and credit unions to expand access to affordable credit through technology that’s both radically intelligent and deeply human. Our platform runs over one million predictions per borrower using more than 3,000 signals, powering smarter, fairer decisions for millions of customers. But the numbers only hint at the impact. Every idea, every voice, and every contribution moves us closer to a world where credit never stands between people and their financial progress.

We’re proudly digital-first, giving most Upstarters the flexibility to do their best work from wherever they thrive, alongside teammates across 80+ cities in the US and Canada. Digital-first doesn’t mean distant. We’re intentional about in-person connection through team onsites, planning sessions, and moments that spark creativity and trust. And whether you choose to work primarily from home or collaborate in-person from one of our offices in Columbus, Austin, the Bay Area, or New York City, you’ll have the support to work in the way that works best for you.

If you’re energized by tackling meaningful problems, excited to innovate with purpose, and motivated by work that truly matters, we’d love to hear from you.

The Team:

Marketing Science sits within Upstart's Growth, Product, and Ops Analytics team and partners with growth marketing on every channel that brings borrowers to Upstart: direct mail, paid search and social, video, mobile, email, brand campaigns, and lending partnerships. Our job is to tell the business which of those dollars are working, and then help decide where the next one goes.

As our Marketing Measurement lead, you'll own how Upstart answers some key questions about its marketing spend. What did each channel actually cause? How should credit be shared across the touches a borrower saw before applying? Where should next quarter's budget go? The answers decide whether a dollar of spend buys a funded loan or takes credit for one that would have arrived anyway.

We're looking for a data scientist with deep experience in causal inference and marketing measurement to be the measurement partner for our marketing, finance, and product leaders, and the person they trust to say when the evidence is strong enough to move the budget.

How you’ll make an impact

• Guide incrementality measurement across our marketing channels, working with the analysts who run tests in each channel on design and interpretation, so the team knows what each channel causes rather than what it gets credit for

• Apply causal inference methods when a clean test isn't feasible, so budget decisions still rest on causal evidence

• Build and maintain the attribution approach that splits credit across direct mail, digital, partnerships, and email, including channels where a borrower never clicks anything

• Turn measurement results into spend allocation recommendations that marketing and finance use to plan budgets

• Use marketing mix models alongside experiments and attribution, and work out which to trust when they disagree

• Automate recurring measurement reporting, so your time goes to interpretation and recommendations

• Mentor analysts across the team and review their measurement work

Minimum Qualifications

• 8+ years of experience in data science or a related quantitative role, much of it spent measuring marketing or growth spend

• Hands-on experience designing and analyzing incrementality tests, and a solid grasp of causal inference beyond standard A/B testing

• Working knowledge of marketing mix modeling and multi-touch attribution, including where each one breaks down

• Strong Python and SQL skills

If you’re energized by tackling meaningful problems, excited to innovate with purpose, and motivated by work that truly matters, we’d love to hear from you.

The Team:

At Upstart, our Applied AI team's mission is threefold:

•
Agent Platform: Build and support the platform that makes it straightforward for non technical users across Upstart to build, launch, and operate AI agents (voice/chat/text) reliably.

Borrower and Applicant Assistant Orchestration: Build the orchestration layer behind a unified personal assistant that shares context across specialized agents, giving applicants and borrowers a cohesive, assistant-like experience.

Borrower-Connected Internal Workflows: Improve internal operational workflows that directly connect to applicant and borrower experiences, making them faster, smarter, and more efficient.

Rather than owning internal developer-tooling infrastructure or training foundation models from scratch, your mandate is to compress the time between an ambiguous idea and a reliable, user-facing AI system, while raising the applied AI bar across every squad you touch.

jobs.description:
Headquarters: San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States

About the role:

Mercury is looking for a Model Risk Manager to help build and operate a practical, risk-based Model Risk Management program as we continue to scale and prepare for life as a regulated bank.

Models support an increasingly broad range of decisions across Mercury, including credit underwriting, portfolio management, fraud prevention, BSA/AML, CECL, finance, liquidity, pricing, and operational processes. This role will provide independent review and effective challenge throughout the model lifecycle while helping Mercury apply governance proportionate to the actual risk of each model.

This is a hands-on role for someone who can move comfortably between technical analysis, regulatory expectations, and business context. You will conduct model validations, challenge assumptions and limitations, improve our model inventory and monitoring practices, and work closely with teams across Risk Ops, Data, Engineering, Product, Finance, Compliance, and Internal Audit.

Showing up as a true collaborator, advisor and partner to the business will be key as we continue to build out this function and work towards our collective goals at Mercury. You should be comfortable operating in a fast-moving environment where the objective is not governance for its own sake, but helping Mercury use models safely, responsibly, and effectively.

What you’ll do:

• Perform independent validations and reviews of internally developed and third-party models across areas such as credit, fraud, BSA/AML, CECL, finance, liquidity, pricing, and operational risk.

• Evaluate each model’s methodology, assumptions, data quality and lineage, implementation, and performance through reviews and testings such as outcomes analysis, benchmarking, back-testing, and sensitivity testing scaled to its risk and materiality.

• Provide credible and constructive challenges to model developers, owners, and users while maintaining effective working relationships with 1LOD.

• Assess model risk and materiality based on a model’s inherent risk, purpose, exposure, use, and potential impact.

• Help maintain a complete and accurate model inventory, including model ownership, risk rating, dependencies, limitations, validation status, monitoring requirements, and open issues.

• Review ongoing monitoring plans and results, including performance thresholds, overrides, data drift, model changes, and conditions that could make a model no longer fit for purpose.

• Evaluate vendor models and other third-party analytical products, including available documentation, transparency, performance, limitations, customization, and Mercury’s ability to monitor and control their use.

• Document validation conclusions clearly, identify issues, recommend proportionate remediation, and track findings through resolution.

• Support controlled model use when validation cannot be completed before implementation by helping establish appropriate limitations, compensating controls, monitoring, and approvals.

• Develop clear reporting on model risk, validation coverage, performance concerns, concentrations, dependencies, exceptions, and overdue remediation for management and governance committees.

• Help improve Mercury’s Model Risk Management Policy, standards, procedures, and templates.

• Use automation and analytical tools to make model inventory management, testing, monitoring, and reporting more efficient.

• Partner with Mercury’s Data and AI Governance teams to establish clear boundaries and handoffs between traditional model risk management and the governance of generative AI, agentic AI, and other analytical systems outside the formal model definition.

• Support regulatory examinations, Internal Audit reviews, and other assurance activities involving model risk.

What we’re looking for:

• 5+ years of relevant experience in model validation, model development, quantitative risk analytics, or a related discipline within banking, fintech, financial services, or consulting.

• Bachelor’s degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science, Engineering, Financial Engineering or a related field. Master’s degree or PhD is preferred.

• Strong knowledge of model risk management principles and current regulatory expectations, including the revised interagency guidance reflected in SR 26-2.

• Intensive experience validating or developing models in one or more areas such as BSA/AML, fraud, financial forecasting, CECL, capital, liquidity, and credit underwriting, using one or more methodologies such as machine learning (e.g., XGBoost, random forests), scorecards, complex vendor models (e.g., Alloy, Firco), and complex spreadsheet-based models.

• Proficiency with SQL and Python (from a data analytics lens); comfortable building understanding of models independently of their developers through collecting evidence and data analytics.

Appointment Setter, Wealth Without Wall Street (Remote)
Read this first. It might save you an hour.
The base on this job is $2,000 a month. It's real, it's guaranteed, and it won't pay your bills by itself. We're not going to pretend it will.
If that made you close the tab, good. We just saved each other some time.
If it made you lean in, here's why the people who win this seat don't care about the base.
30,000 people are sitting in our database. Every one of them raised their hand to learn how to build passive income and become their own bank. Almost nobody is calling them.
That's your seat.
Who we are: Russ Morgan and Joey Muré have been teaching business owners how money actually works since 2015. They wrote the book on it, literally. And they don't just teach it. Every month they publish their own passive income in public. Most money teachers won't show you their numbers. Ours put theirs out every month.
What you'll actually do

You'll call warm leads. No bought lists and no cold calling.

• About 200 new leads come in every month from our webinars and referrals.

• Behind them are 30,000 people who know our name and haven't heard from us in a while. Some raised a hand this morning and some a year ago.

• You book qualified calls for our closers, and you follow up like it matters, because it does.

Here's the catch. These are business owners, and plenty of them have read the book. Read a script at them and they'll eat you alive. You have to actually understand what you're talking about.
That's the part no other sales job will give you. While we pay you to make these calls, you learn the same system our clients pay to learn: how to stop handing your money to the banks and how to build income that keeps coming in. You'll use it on the phone, and then you'll use it in your own life.

The math (check it yourself)

• $2,000 monthly base

• $50 to $100 for every appointment that shows

• About $300 for every sale that closes from your bookings

20 closes a month is $6,000 in commission. Add the $2,000 base and you're at $8,000 before appointment pay. That's what this seat is built to produce.
You won't get there in your first month. The early stretch is leaner while you learn the system and build your pipeline. Setters who win treat that stretch as an investment. Setters who wash out treat it as a paycheck.
Where this goes: We're filling closing seats too. They go to whoever earns them, and the fastest way to earn one is from this chair.

You'll fit if:

• You've spent 1 to 2 years on the phone somewhere real: solar, door to door, appointment setting, insurance, high-ticket, inside sales or home services

• You can hold your ground with a business owner who pushes back, 50 times a day

• You can make 150 dials without hunting for a shortcut

• When you get coaching, tomorrow's call sounds different

• You follow up without being reminded

• You've worked in a CRM (HubSpot is a plus)

• You have reliable internet and a quiet, professional home office

Please don't apply if:

• You want the base to carry you and see commission as a bonus

• You've hopped between 3 or more sales jobs in the last 2 years

• You go quiet when a buyer who's read the book pushes back

• You need someone watching you to stay on the phone at 4pm

What winning looks like here: you hit your dials every day, call new leads fast, book qualified appointments, use coaching the same day you get it and own your number.

Compensation This is a performance-based opportunity that rewards consistency and execution.

• $2,000 monthly base, plus $50 to $100 per held appointment and about $300 per closed sale

• Typical on-target earnings of $6,000 to $10,000 a month once you're ramped

• Warm inbound leads, with zero cold lists

• Fully remote

• Real onboarding and ongoing coaching from experienced sales leaders

• A clear path into closing and sales leadership

• You learn the wealth system our clients pay to learn, on the clock

• An established company that has been teaching this since 2015

Actual earnings depend on individual performance and are not guaranteed.

This is a remote position with travel required. You may be based anywhere.

Appleseed is building a team of seasoned behavioral strategists who are also skilled researchers and client partners. This is not an academic or theoretical role: our consultants deliver B2B client services, leading field-driven research and crafting human-centered strategies that stick. We work only with nonprofits and funders fighting poverty and protecting the planet. This role requires behavioral insight, leadership & storytelling ability, and a deep commitment to continuous learning.

We are seeking to fill both full-time core team and freelance project lead roles with significant ownership and influence in shaping Appleseed’s craft and culture. We are excited to meet exceptional candidates who prefer ongoing project-based work, as well as those who would rather join the core team full-time.

• Co-founder of a startup that achieved product-market fit

We are especially eager to meet people with proven strength in field-based research, behavioral diagnosis and strategy, or storytelling — even if your title has never said “design.”

• Synthesis: Synthesizing motivators and barriers into behavioral diagnoses using Appleseed’s methodology, similar to COM-B, EAST, CBSM, or Fogg.

• Deliverables & Storytelling: Crafting clear, persuasive, narrative-driven strategy deliverables — frameworks, visuals, decision-making tools, and client playbooks — and telling stories that move clients to act.

Your charter includes our content management systems, telesales technology, member app, and public surface area including our enrollment forms and customer data and public analytics platforms. You will work through the whole chain, from a data source or API to what an agent or prospective member actually experiences.

• Work directly with sales, growth, marketing, and operating partners to understand the business problem, choose useful increments, and agree how their value will be measured.

• Connect analytics, leads, customer data, CRM, and operating workflows. Make data flows, ownership, and failure behavior understandable and dependable.

• Build and improve software personally. Use AI in development, investigation, analysis, prototypes, and useful product capabilities, and evaluate the result against actual behavior.

• First six months: The team has landed a new telesales stack, and other agreed acquisition priorities, including the ongoing growth demands of a five star Medicare Advantage plan. • You have strong product instincts and can translate a commercial or operating goal into a useful technical plan with measurable results.

• You have built systems involving customer data, CRM, sales or acquisition workflows, public web and content management experiences, or similarly interconnected operations.

• You use AI deeply in your own engineering work and have practical experience building or integrating AI-backed capabilities. You can explain how you check the result.

• You work well with business partners, make tradeoffs clear, and can move work forward when the initial request is ambiguous.

We encourage you to help us break that statistic!

About Tailscale

Tailscale is making safe connection effortless by delivering software that makes it easy to securely interconnect people and their devices, no matter where they are. From hobbyists to multinational corporations, teams of every size use Tailscale each day to protect their networks, share access to internal tools, and more. We're building a future for the Internet that's easy, sensible, and safe, like it used to be. Founded in 2019 and fully distributed, we're backed by Accel, CRV, Insight, Heavybit, and Uncork Capital.

About the Role

If you're passionate about solving complex technical problems and helping build trust between customers and engineering, this is the role for you. We're seeking a motivated Customer Reliability Engineer to join our team. You'll take ownership of our most complex, ambiguous customer escalations, solving issues where the root cause is not always obvious. You will work these issues to resolution or alternatively a fully-documented handoff that engineering can act on without delay.

As a Customer Reliability Engineer, you'll partner closely with the Customer Success Team, Support Team, and Product/Engineering to close the gap between "customer has described a problem" and "engineering has what it needs to fix it." This role reports directly to the Customer Reliability Engineer Team Lead.

Key Responsibilities

• Own high-severity, post-sales technical escalations from intake through resolution or engineering handoff. This includes deep-dive investigations and reproduction of difficult-to-isolate bugs.

• Get on calls with customers, pull logs, and communicate with the customer about leading theories.

• Build engineering handoff packages that require minimal follow-up questions: reproducible case, log evidence (timestamps, node IDs), version matrix, impact scope, what's already been ruled out, and a proposed engineering team to own the fix.

• File and track issues for confirmed bugs, keeping the ticket/issue link intact so engineering retains full customer context.

• Monitor for patterns across escalations to catch recurring or systemic issues early; translate what you learn into product improvements, tooling, and runbooks that raise the technical bar for the whole Support org.

• Partner with Support, CSE, and Product/Eng, while staying within this team's scope.

What We Are Looking For

• 4+ years in a technical support or escalation role at a SaaS or infrastructure company, with demonstrated ownership of escalated/enterprise-tier accounts.

• A genuine problem-solver who gets energy from untangling hard, ambiguous technical issues

• Comfortable owning a live, high-stakes customer call: staying calm, building trust, and communicating clearly with a frustrated or technical customer under pressure.

• Hands-on networking experience in production or homelab environments: TCP/IP, routing, DNS, firewalls, NAT, VPNs, load balancers.

• Deep familiarity with overlay networking concepts — WireGuard, UDP hole punching, STUN — and comparable VPN/networking products.

• Code-level debugging capability: can read Go source, reason about goroutines/locks/channels, read pprof CPU/heap profiles, and understand network interface semantics.

• Comfortable with infrastructure concepts: cloud IaaS, CI/CD pipelines, containerized applications, and Kubernetes debugging.

• Strong systems administration skills as well as troubleshooting across Linux, macOS, and Windows.

• Track record of independently building reproducible test cases and clear, evidence-backed bug reports engineering can act on directly.

• Strong technical storytelling: able to distill highly technical, ambiguous issues into clear narratives for both engineers and non-technical stakeholders.

• Investigative mindset; curious to analyze root cause, and evaluate all options to get customers to the best solution

• Proficiency with programming/scripting in Go, Python, JSON

• Experience with packet-level analysis

Backed by Y Combinator and Sequoia Capital, Magic has spent 10+ years connecting fast-growing businesses with top remote talent.

Our clients are busy founders and executives who need remote workers to deliver real ROI, and they need a strategic partner to make that happen. You're not here to answer tickets. You're here to protect revenue, grow accounts, and turn happy clients into loud advocates. Key Responsibilities

•
Guard your book of business: own a portfolio of accounts sorted by size, health, and growth potential, and hold 90%+ gross revenue retention (GRR) and 110%+ net revenue retention (NRR). Those are the numbers you're graded on.

•
Spot at-risk accounts before clients say a word. Start renewals 60–90 days out, and get save plans moving early.

•
Launch every new client fast: kickoff call within 24–48 hours of signing, then Magic's 30-60-90 day onboarding framework, with a success plan tied to their business goals and an intro to their remote worker.

•
Host quarterly business reviews (QBRs) clients actually look forward to: data-driven, strategic, action-oriented. Become the trusted advisor to founders and C-suite, and multi-thread across each client so one champion leaving doesn't sink the account.

•
Hunt expansion opportunities and make the business case before anyone asks.

•
Surface the story in the data: track churn risk and expansion signals, keep HubSpot clean, send a monthly portfolio health report (retention, NRR, CSAT, NPS, QBR completion), and own every escalation from intake to resolution.

Qualifications & Technical Requirements

• 3+ years of B2B customer success or account management experience, juggling a portfolio of accounts at the same time

• Direct ownership of revenue retention and expansion targets across the full customer lifecycle from onboarding to renewal

• Background in SaaS/tech, outsourcing/staffing, professional services/BPO, or marketplace platforms

• HubSpot experience used daily for pipeline and account health (intermediate-to-expert Salesforce or a similar CRM also works)

• Intermediate-to-advanced Excel or Google Sheets: pivot tables, VLOOKUP/INDEX MATCH, dashboards, trend analysis

• Real US market experience: you know US business culture, SMB challenges, and how executives like to communicate

• Strong written and spoken English, good enough for daily conversations with US-based C-level and Director clients

• A professional home office: high-speed internet (50+ Mbps), a headset, and a quiet space

You treat customer success as a revenue function, not a help desk. You own the outcome, so you don't wait to be told an account is wobbling; you've already spotted it, and your save plan is moving.
